info.title: Agent Graph API
info.summary: Read the graphs your coding agents make, at any point in their history.
info.description:
The Agent Graph API gives your own servers, and the AI systems they run, read access to the graphs your coding agents make: every session and subagent, what each is doing, who is waiting on whom, and how that changed over time.

It is a REST API with predictable, resource-oriented URLs. It returns JSON, uses standard HTTP verbs, status codes and authentication, and is read-only: every endpoint is a `GET`.

~~~bash
curl https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs \
  -u ag_sk_live_51Hx7Qm2Vb9Kd4Tz0Ws3Ne8LrPq4Xa9T:
~~~

## What's in a graph

A **graph** is one of your account's live shares: what `agent-graph watch-remote` streams from your machine. It holds **nodes** and the **events** that made them.

- A **node** is a session (one run of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) or an agent that a session or another agent started. Nodes form trees: every node has a `parent_id`, a `root_id` (the top of its tree) and a `session_id` (the session it runs in).
- An **event** is one thing that happened: a session started, an agent was spawned, a node changed state, a task list was updated. Events are immutable and ordered; each one records which nodes it changed, and how.

The graph is derived from the events by the same reducer the viewer runs, so the API and the viewer always agree.

## Authentication

Authenticate with an API key, made on your [account page](https://agentgraph.chofter.com/account). Send it as the username of HTTP Basic auth (no password), or as a bearer token:

~~~bash
curl https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ag_sk_live_51Hx7Qm2Vb9Kd4Tz0Ws3Ne8LrPq4Xa9T"
~~~

| Prefix | Kind | Can read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ag_sk_live_` | Secret key | Every graph your account owns |
| `ag_rk_live_` | Restricted key | Only the graphs chosen when it was made |

Keys are shown once, when made, and stored only as a hash: keep them secret, on your server, never in a browser or a repository. Revoke a key on the account page and it stops working at once. All requests must be made over HTTPS.

## Versioning

The API is versioned by date. Each key is pinned to the version current when it was made, so a change that would break your integration never reaches you unannounced. To try another version for one request, send it in the `Agent-Graph-Version` header; every response says which version answered it.

~~~bash
curl https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs \
  -u ag_sk_live_51Hx7Qm2Vb9Kd4Tz0Ws3Ne8LrPq4Xa9T: \
  -H "Agent-Graph-Version: 2026-10-09"
~~~

Adding a field, an endpoint, an optional parameter, an event type, an enum value or an error code is not a breaking change. Your code should ignore what it doesn't recognise.

## Ids

Every object has an `id` with a prefix that says what it is.

| Object | Prefix | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Graph | `gph_` | `gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a` |
| Node | `node_` | `node_Y2xhdWRlLWNvZGU6NWYyYzFlOWE…` |
| Event | `evt_` | `evt_01M4G2FMPN7KD3N1PZ0QX8RM4A` |

- A **graph** id is `gph_` and the id in the share's link: `/l/k3P9xQ2mWt7a` is `gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a`.
- A **node** id is `node_` and the base64url (no padding) of the id the agent tool gave it, which is returned as `provider_ref`: `claude-code:<session>` for a session, `claude-code:<session>/<agent>` for an agent. The encoding is reversible, needs no lookup, and keeps ids safe in a URL path.
- An **event** id is `evt_` and the event's ULID. ULIDs sort by time, so event ids sort in the order events happened, and any event id names a point in time (below).

Ids are case-sensitive. Treat them as opaque strings: don't parse them, except to decode `node_` ids if you need the provider's own id and don't have `provider_ref` at hand.

## Time travel: `as_of`

Every graph, node and search endpoint can answer as of any point in the graph's retained history. Pass `as_of`:

| Value | Answers with |
| --- | --- |
| An event id, `evt_…` | The state just after that event was applied |
| A Unix time in milliseconds | The state after the last event at or before that time |
| Omitted | The state now |

Every object and list in a response carries `as_of_event_id`: the event it was answered at. Pass it on later requests to read one consistent moment, even while the graph keeps changing:

~~~bash
# What's stuck right now?
curl -G https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs/gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a/nodes \
  -u $AGENT_GRAPH_KEY: -d stale=true
# → "as_of_event_id": "evt_01M4G3G4E8Q9R2M5X4T6W8Y0B1"

# Everything under the first one, at that same moment.
curl -G https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs/gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a/nodes/node_Y2xhdWRlLWNvZGU6NWYyYzFlOWEtOGQxYi00YjZlLTlhNTEtMGY2ZjJjN2QzZTEwL2I4MWMyMmUwOWY3YTNjNTU \
  -u $AGENT_GRAPH_KEY: \
  -d as_of=evt_01M4G3G4E8Q9R2M5X4T6W8Y0B1 \
  -d "expand[]=descendants"
~~~

A response for a fixed point never changes, so it's sent with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

To walk through history rather than look at one point, list [events](#tag/Events): each records which nodes it changed, field by field.

## Retention

A live share keeps its recent history: between 1,000 and 2,000 events, trimmed from the start as new ones arrive. A graph's `retention` says what it holds now. An `as_of` before `retention.first_event_id` is refused with `410` and the code `outside_retention_window`, and the error names the oldest point you can ask for.

When a share restarts on a new machine state (see `restart` in the [design notes](https://agentgraph.chofter.com/docs)), its retained history can briefly shrink to less than 1,000 events.

## Ids versus objects, and expanding

A field that refers to another object comes in two forms, and they never mix:

- `parent_id`, `root_id`, `session_id`, `requested_by_id`, `on_ids`, …: **always** a string id (or `null`, or an array of ids), and **always** present.
- `parent`, `root`, `session`, `requested_by`, `on`, …: **always** the full object, and present **only** when you ask for it with `expand[]`. A field that wasn't expanded is absent, never an id in its place.

So a field never changes type, and whether something was expanded is simply whether its field is there.

~~~bash
curl -G https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs/gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a/nodes/node_Y2xhdWRlLWNvZGU6NWYyYzFlOWEtOGQxYi00YjZlLTlhNTEtMGY2ZjJjN2QzZTEwL2EzZmQwN2MyYjE5ZTRkNjE \
  -u $AGENT_GRAPH_KEY: \
  -d "expand[]=parent" \
  -d "expand[]=children"
~~~

Some fields exist only when expanded, because they can be large: `children`, `descendants`, `tasks`, `spawns`, `waits` and `messages`.

**Paths.** Expand an expanded object's fields with dots: `expand[]=parent.parent`, `expand[]=children.children`, `expand[]=blocked.on`. A path goes at most **4 levels** deep, and a request can expand at most 20 paths. In a list, expand each item's fields with the `data.` prefix: `expand[]=data.parent`.

**Whole subtrees.** `children` is nested, one level per path segment. For everything under a node, however deep, expand `descendants` instead: a single flat list in tree order, each node with its `parent_id`, paged like any other list. See [Retrieve a node](#operation/retrieveNode).

## Pagination

Every list endpoint returns a list object and takes the same cursor parameters:

~~~json
{
  "object": "list",
  "url": "/api/v1/graphs/gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a/nodes",
  "as_of_event_id": "evt_01M4G3G4E8Q9R2M5X4T6W8Y0B1",
  "has_more": true,
  "data": [ … ]
}
~~~

| Parameter | |
| --- | --- |
| `limit` | How many objects to return, 1 to 1,000. Defaults to 100. |
| `starting_after` | An object id: return the page after it. Pass the last `id` of the page you have. |
| `ending_before` | An object id: return the page before it. Pass the first `id` of the page you have. |

Keep `as_of` the same across the pages of one list (the first page's `as_of_event_id`), so that nodes added in the meantime don't shift the pages under you. An embedded list's `url` already includes it, and every parameter that defined the list: add only `starting_after`.

[Search](#operation/searchNodes) pages with `page` and `next_page` instead, as its results are ranked.

## Conditional requests

Every successful response has an `ETag`. Send it back as `If-None-Match` and, if nothing has changed, you get `304 Not Modified` with no body. That's the cheap way to poll the state now: it costs no rate limit and almost no bandwidth.

Responses are compressed with Brotli or gzip when you send `Accept-Encoding`.

## Errors

The API uses conventional HTTP status codes: `2xx` succeeded, `4xx` means something about the request was wrong, `5xx` means something went wrong on our side (they're rare). Every error has the same shape:

~~~json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "outside_retention_window",
    "message": "This graph holds events from evt_01M4FXYWR82B8XK0V5QJ7M1N3R to evt_01M4G3G4E8Q9R2M5X4T6W8Y0B1.",
    "param": "as_of",
    "doc_url": "https://agentgraph.chofter.com/docs/reference#errors",
    "first_event_id": "evt_01M4FXYWR82B8XK0V5QJ7M1N3R",
    "last_event_id": "evt_01M4G3G4E8Q9R2M5X4T6W8Y0B1"
  }
}
~~~

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK. |
| `304` | Not modified since the `ETag` you sent. |
| `400` | A parameter is missing, unknown or invalid. |
| `401` | No API key, or one that's invalid or revoked. |
| `403` | The key can't read this graph. |
| `404` | No such graph, node or event, or the node doesn't exist at `as_of`. |
| `410` | `as_of` is older than the graph's retained history. |
| `429` | Too many requests: wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `500`, `502`, `503` | Something went wrong on our side. Safe to retry: every request is read-only. |

| Type | |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | The request was invalid. |
| `authentication_error` | The API key is missing, invalid or revoked. |
| `permission_error` | The key isn't allowed to do this. |
| `rate_limit_error` | Too many requests. |
| `api_error` | Something went wrong on our side. |

| Code | Status | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parameter_missing` | 400 | A required parameter is missing. `param` names it. |
| `parameter_invalid` | 400 | A parameter's value is invalid. `param` names it. |
| `parameter_unknown` | 400 | A parameter that the endpoint doesn't take. `param` names it. |
| `version_invalid` | 400 | `Agent-Graph-Version` isn't a version. |
| `expand_invalid` | 400 | An `expand[]` path names a field that can't be expanded. |
| `expand_too_deep` | 400 | An `expand[]` path goes more than 4 levels deep. |
| `expand_not_allowed` | 400 | That expansion isn't available here: `descendants` and `children` can't be expanded on the items of a list. |
| `search_query_invalid` | 400 | The search query couldn't be parsed. `message` says where. |
| `api_key_missing` | 401 | No API key was sent. |
| `api_key_invalid` | 401 | The API key isn't one, or has been revoked. |
| `api_key_restricted` | 403 | A restricted key that can't read this graph. |
| `resource_missing` | 404 | No such graph, node or event (for this key). |
| `node_not_yet_created` | 404 | The node exists, but not yet at `as_of`. `first_event_id` is the event that creates it. |
| `outside_retention_window` | 410 | `as_of` is before the graph's retained history. `first_event_id` and `last_event_id` say what it holds. |
| `rate_limit` | 429 | Too many requests. |
| `api_error` | 500 | Something went wrong on our side. |

Every response, including errors, has a `Request-Id` header. Include it if you contact us about a request.

## Rate limits

Each key can make 25 requests a second, in bursts of up to 100. Responses carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the limit resets); a refused request has `Retry-After`. A `304` doesn't count.

The limit is kept by each of the site's servers, so a key whose requests are spread over several can go a little faster. Don't rely on it: keep to the limit.

The cheapest way to follow a graph is to list [events](#tag/Events) `starting_after` the last one you saw, or to poll with `If-None-Match`, not to fetch the whole graph again.

## Text in nodes is untrusted

Fields like `title`, `summary`, `headline`, `purpose`, `attention`, task text and message summaries are written by coding agents, from what they were working on. They can contain anything, including text written to manipulate a model that reads it.

If you pass them to an AI system, mark them as data, not instructions, and don't let them trigger actions on their own.

## What's not included

- **Prompts.** No endpoint returns what a person typed to an agent.
- **Message bodies** are present only if the share was made with body capture on; otherwise `body` is `null`.
- **Processes and hosts.** The ids of processes and the names of machines are left out.

tags.name: Graphs
tags.description:
A graph is one of your account's live shares: the sessions and agents `agent-graph watch-remote` streams from a machine, kept on the site while it's in use, and deleted after a week with no new events.

Retrieve a graph to see what it holds (`retention`), how big it is, and how its nodes stand (`counts`), now or as of any retained event.

tags.name: Nodes
tags.description:
A node is a session (one run of a coding agent) or an agent it started. Nodes form trees:

~~~
session        claude-code:5f2c1e…            depth 0, parent_id null
├─ agent       claude-code:5f2c1e…/a3fd07…    depth 1
│  └─ agent    claude-code:5f2c1e…/b81c22…    depth 2
└─ agent       claude-code:5f2c1e…/c90d13…    depth 1
~~~

Every node says where it sits: `parent_id`, `root_id` (the top of its tree, following sessions that started other sessions), `session_id` (the session it runs in) and `depth`.

**State.** A node's `state` is one of:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `working` | Doing something. |
| `input_required` | Waiting on a person: a permission prompt, a question, a plan to approve. `attention` says what's asked. |
| `idle` | A session whose turn is over, alive and waiting for its next prompt. |
| `completed` | Finished. |
| `failed` | Finished with an error. |
| `canceled` | Stopped before it finished. |

Waiting on another node isn't a state: a node can be `working` and `blocked` at once. `blocked` says what it's waiting on, directly (`on_ids`) and in all (how many nodes, how many open tasks among them), and whether the waits form a cycle that can never finish. A `working` node with no events for 30 minutes, and nothing it's waiting on, is `stale`: it may have hung or crashed.

tags.name: Events
tags.description:
An event is one thing that happened in a graph. Events are immutable and ordered by `id`, which sorts by time.

Each event has the `payload` its agent tool reported, and `changes`: every node the event changed, and for each, the fields that changed, from what to what. A node's derived fields count too: an agent being spawned changes its parent's `child_count`, and every ancestor's `descendant_count`.

List events `starting_after` the last one you saw to follow a graph cheaply, or with `order=asc` from any point to replay its history.

**Event types**

| Type | `payload` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.started` | `cwd?`, `source?` (`startup`, `resume`, …), `title?`, `link_method?` | A session starts or resumes. |
| `session.ended` | `reason?` | A session exits. |
| `agent.spawned` | `agent_type?`, `purpose?`, `background?` | An agent starts. |
| `agent.finished` | `status` (`completed`, `failed`, `canceled`), `summary?` | An agent stops. |
| `status` | `state`, `summary?`, `title?` | A node's state or status line changes. |
| `tasks.updated` | `items`: `[{id, text, active_text?, status}]` | A to-do tool sent its whole list, which replaces the node's. |
| `task.upserted` | `id`, `text?`, `active_text?`, `status?` | One task was created or changed. |
| `task.deleted` | `id` | A task was removed. |
| `spawn.requested` | `call_id`, `kind` (`agent`, `session`), `agent_type?`, `purpose?`, `background` | A node asked for a child to start. Unless `background`, it's blocked until the call returns. |
| `spawn.returned` | `call_id`, `child?`, `outcome?` | That call returned. |
| `wait.started` | `wait_id`, `on` (a provider node id), `reason?` | A node blocked on another for some other reason. |
| `wait.ended` | `wait_id`, `outcome?` | That block cleared. |
| `message.sent` | `message_id`, `to`, `reply_to?`, `summary?`, `body?` | One node sent another a message. |
| `activity` | `tool`, `label?` | A tool call, when the share records them. |

Ids inside `payload` are the provider's own (as in `provider_ref`), exactly as the agent tool reported them; use `node_id` and `changes` for API ids. More types may be added: ignore those you don't recognise.

get.description:
Returns the graphs this key can read: your account's live shares, most recently active first.

Each graph's `counts` are as of its own latest event.

parameters.name: last_event
parameters.description: Only graphs whose latest event is in this range. `last_event[gte]=<5 minutes ago>` lists the shares active now.

schema.description: A range of times, in Unix milliseconds. Send any of `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte`.

get.description:
Retrieves a graph: what history it holds (`retention`) and how its nodes stand (`counts`), now or as of any retained event.

This is the cheapest overview of a graph: one small object however many nodes it has. Poll it with `If-None-Match` to learn when anything changes.

Returns a graph's nodes as of a point in its history, filtered and ordered as you ask.

Common uses:

| To list | Send |
| --- | --- |
| The top-level trees | `is_root=true` |
| A node's children | `parent_id=node_…` |
| Everything under a node | `ancestor_id=node_…&order=tree` |
| The top three levels under it | `ancestor_id=node_…&max_depth=3&order=tree` |
| Everything waiting on a person | `state=input_required` |
| What may have hung | `stale=true` |
| What's blocked behind another node | `blocked=true` |

Filters combine with AND. In tree order (`order=tree`), each parent comes before its children, and siblings are oldest first, so a page never separates a node from what places it; with a filter, the nodes that match keep that order.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Fields to expand on each node, with the `data.` prefix: `expand[]=data.parent`, `expand[]=data.blocked.on`. `children` and `descendants` can't be expanded in a list (use `parent_id` or `ancestor_id` instead).

Send one `expand[]` per path. A path goes at most 4 levels deep; at most 20 paths per request. An expanded field appears beside its `_id` field, which is always there; one not expanded is absent.

parameters.name: parent_id
parameters.description: Only nodes directly under this one.

parameters.name: ancestor_id
parameters.description: Only nodes under this one, at any depth (not the node itself).

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.description: With `ancestor_id`: only nodes at most this many levels below it. 1 is its children.

parameters.name: root_id
parameters.description: Only nodes in this tree, the root included.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Only this session and the agents in it.

parameters.name: is_root
parameters.description: Only roots (`true`) or only non-roots (`false`).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only sessions or only agents.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only nodes in these states. Send one `state[]` per state.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Only nodes from this agent tool, e.g. `claude-code`.

parameters.name: agent_type
parameters.description: Only agents of this type, e.g. `Explore`.

parameters.name: stale
parameters.description: Only nodes that are, or aren't, `stale`.

parameters.name: blocked
parameters.description: Only nodes that are (`true`) or aren't (`false`) waiting on another node.

parameters.name: created
parameters.description: Only nodes that started in this range.

schema.description: A range of start times, in Unix milliseconds. Send any of `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte`.

parameters.name: last_event
parameters.description: Only nodes whose last event is in this range.

schema.description: A range of times, in Unix milliseconds. Send any of `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `newest`: most recently started first. `tree`: depth-first, each parent before its children, siblings oldest first.

get.description:
Searches a graph's nodes with a query, as of a point in its history.

Use it for questions the [list filters](#operation/listNodes) can't express: text in a node's summary, OR, negation, numeric comparisons.

**Query language**

A query is one or more clauses, joined by `AND` or `OR` (not both in one query). Values are quoted.

| Clause | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `field:"value"` | Exactly equal (case-insensitive for text). |
| `field~"value"` | Contains (text fields; at least 3 characters). |
| `-field:"value"` | Not equal. |
| `field>value`, `field>=value`, `field<value`, `field<=value` | Numbers and times (Unix milliseconds). |
| `field:null` | Has no value. |

**Fields:** `state`, `kind`, `provider`, `agent_type`, `stale`, `blocked`, `background`, `parent_id`, `root_id`, `session_id`, `depth`, `created`, `ended`, `last_event`, `child_count`, `descendant_count`, `open_tasks` (its `task_counts.open`), `blocked_open_tasks` (its `blocked.open_tasks`), `title`, `summary`, `headline`, `purpose`, `attention`.

**Examples**

~~~
state:"working" AND stale:"true"
agent_type:"Explore" AND descendant_count>10
state:"failed" OR state:"canceled"
summary~"migration" AND -state:"completed"
blocked_open_tasks>=20
~~~

Results are most recently active first.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search query. See the query language above.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Fields to expand on each node, with the `data.` prefix: `expand[]=data.root`.

Send one `expand[]` per path. A path goes at most 4 levels deep; at most 20 paths per request. An expanded field appears beside its `_id` field, which is always there; one not expanded is absent.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The cursor for a page after the first: the previous page's `next_page`.

get.description:
Retrieves a node as it stood at a point in its graph's history, with whatever around it you expand.

**Expandable fields**

| Path | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `parent` | The parent node, beside `parent_id`. Absent for a root. |
| `root` | The root node, beside `root_id`. |
| `session` | The session node, beside `session_id`. |
| `requested_by` | The node that asked for this one, beside `requested_by_id`. |
| `blocked.on` | The nodes it's waiting on, beside `blocked.on_ids`. |
| `children` | Its children, as a list (the first 100, oldest first, and a `url` for the rest). |
| `descendants` | Every node under it, as one flat list in tree order (the first 1,000, and a `url` for the rest). See `descendants_max_depth`. |
| `tasks` | Its task list. |
| `spawns` | The children it has asked for. |
| `waits` | What it has waited on, and is waiting on. |
| `messages` | Messages it has sent and received. |

Expanded nodes can be expanded in turn: `parent.parent`, `children.children`, `root.tasks`.

**Expanding to a depth.** `expand[]=children.children` nests two levels of children; a path goes at most 4 levels.

**Expanding all the way down.** `expand[]=descendants` returns everything under the node as one flat list, in tree order (each parent before its children), each node with its `parent_id` so you can rebuild the tree in one pass. Limit its depth with `descendants_max_depth`. It holds the first 1,000; if `has_more`, its `url` lists the rest (it includes `as_of`, so every page is the same moment): request it with `starting_after` set to the last node you have.

~~~bash
# The whole tree under a node…
curl -G https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs/gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a/nodes/node_Y2xhdWRlLWNvZGU6NWY… \
  -u $AGENT_GRAPH_KEY: -d "expand[]=descendants"

# …and, if has_more, the next 1,000.
curl -G "https://agentgraph.chofter.com/api/v1/graphs/gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a/nodes?ancestor_id=…&as_of=…&order=tree" \
  -u $AGENT_GRAPH_KEY: -d limit=1000 -d starting_after=node_…
~~~

If the node doesn't exist at `as_of` but does later, the error is `404 node_not_yet_created`, with the event that creates it.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Fields to expand. See `Expandable fields` above.

Send one `expand[]` per path. A path goes at most 4 levels deep; at most 20 paths per request. An expanded field appears beside its `_id` field, which is always there; one not expanded is absent.

parameters.name: descendants_max_depth
parameters.description: With `expand[]=descendants`: only include nodes at most this many levels below. Leave it out for all of them.

get.description:
Returns a graph's events, newest first by default, from its retained history.

**Following a graph.** Remember the newest event id you've seen, and list with `order=asc` and `starting_after` set to it: you get only what's happened since, each event with its `changes`. No need to fetch the graph again. If you fall so far behind that the event is no longer retained, that's `410 outside_retention_window`, and the error's `first_event_id` is the oldest event still held: fetch the graph again, and follow on from there.

**Replaying history.** List with `order=asc` from the start of `retention`, or from any event; `expand[]=data.node` adds each event's node as it stood just after it.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only events of these types. Send one `type[]` per type; a trailing `*` matches a family: `type[]=agent.*`.

parameters.name: node_id
parameters.description: Only events about this node.

parameters.name: root_id
parameters.description: Only events about nodes in this tree.

parameters.name: created
parameters.description: Only events that happened in this range.

schema.description: A range of times, in Unix milliseconds. Send any of `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `desc`: newest first. `asc`: oldest first.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Fields to expand on each event: `expand[]=data.node` (the node just after the event), and its own fields, `data.node.parent`.

Send one `expand[]` per path. A path goes at most 4 levels deep; at most 20 paths per request. An expanded field appears beside its `_id` field, which is always there; one not expanded is absent.

payload.purpose: Find every caller of the old session store

get.description: Retrieves one event, with every change it made. `expand[]=node` adds its node as it stood just after it. An event older than the graph's retained history is `410 outside_retention_window`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Fields to expand: `node`, and its own fields, `node.parent`.

Send one `expand[]` per path. A path goes at most 4 levels deep; at most 20 paths per request. An expanded field appears beside its `_id` field, which is always there; one not expanded is absent.

BearerAuth.description: Your API key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer ag_sk_live_…`. The API also takes it as the username of HTTP Basic auth, with no password (`curl -u ag_sk_live_…:`).

GraphId.name: graph_id
GraphId.description: The graph's id, `gph_…`. The id in a share's link works too: `/l/k3P9xQ2mWt7a` is `gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a`.

AsOf.name: as_of
AsOf.description:
Answer as of this point in the graph's history: an event id (`evt_…`, the state just after that event) or a Unix time in milliseconds (the state after the last event at or before it). Leave it out for now.

Must be within the graph's `retention`, else `410 outside_retention_window`. To read several pages or objects at one moment, pass the `as_of_event_id` of the first response.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: How many objects to return, from 1 to 1,000.

StartingAfter.name: starting_after
StartingAfter.description: A cursor: an object id from the list. Returns the page after it. Pass the last `id` of the page you have to get the next one.

EndingBefore.name: ending_before
EndingBefore.description: A cursor: an object id from the list. Returns the page before it. Pass the first `id` of the page you have to get the previous one.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: The `ETag` of a response you have. If nothing has changed, the reply is `304 Not Modified`, with no body.

Request-Id.description: A unique id for this request, `req_…`. Include it if you contact us about a request.

Agent-Graph-Version.description: The API version that answered the request.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests this key may make each second.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

ETag.description: An opaque version of this response. Send it back as `If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified` while it's unchanged.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

BadRequest.description: The request was invalid: a parameter is missing, unknown or invalid, or an expansion isn't allowed.

error.message: Invalid limit: must be between 1 and 1000.
The path children.children.children.children.children goes 5 levels deep; at most 4 are allowed.

Unauthorized.description: No API key was sent, or the one sent is invalid or revoked.

Forbidden.description: The API key can't read this graph.

error.message: This restricted key can't read gph_k3P9xQ2mWt7a.

NotFound.description: No such object for this key, or the node doesn't exist yet at `as_of`.

error.message: The node node_Y2xhdWRlLWNvZGU6NWYyYzFlOWEtOGQxYi00YjZlLTlhNTEtMGY2ZjJjN2QzZTEwL2EzZmQwN2MyYjE5ZTRkNjE is created by evt_01M4G2FMPN7KD3N1PZ0QX8RM4A, after as_of.

Gone.description: `as_of` is before the graph's retained history.

error.message: This graph holds events from evt_01M4FXYWR82B8XK0V5QJ7M1N3R to evt_01M4G3G4E8Q9R2M5X4T6W8Y0B1.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

error.message: Too many requests. Try again in 1 second.

ServerError.description: Something went wrong on our side. Every request is read-only, so it's safe to retry.

error.message: Something went wrong. Try again, and include the Request-Id if it keeps happening.

NotModified.description: Nothing has changed since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`. There's no body, and the request doesn't count towards the rate limit.

NodeState.description:
What a node is doing.

- `working`: doing something.
- `input_required`: waiting on a person (`attention` says what for).
- `idle`: a session between turns, waiting for its next prompt.
- `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`: finished.

NodeKind.description: `session`: one run of a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …). `agent`: an agent started inside a session, by it or by another agent.

Graph.title: Graph
Graph.description: One of your account's live shares, and how its nodes stand at `as_of_event_id`.

object.description: String representing the object's type: always `graph`.

as_of_event_id.description: The event this graph's `counts` are as of. Pass it as `as_of` to read other objects at the same moment.

source.description: How the graph was shared. `watch` is a live share from `agent-graph watch-remote`; this version of the API returns only those.

url.description: Where to see the graph in the viewer. Only the account that owns it can open it.

created.description: When the share was made, in Unix milliseconds.

last_event.description: When its most recent event happened, in Unix milliseconds.

Retention.title: Retention
Retention.description: The span of history the site holds for this graph now, and so the range `as_of` can take. A live share keeps between 1,000 and 2,000 events, trimmed from the start as new ones arrive.

first_event_id.description: The oldest event you can read, or ask `as_of`. `null` while the graph has no events.

last_event_id.description: The newest event. `null` while the graph has no events.

first_event_created.description: When the oldest event happened, in Unix milliseconds.

last_event_created.description: When the newest event happened, in Unix milliseconds.

GraphCounts.title: Graph counts
GraphCounts.description: How many nodes the graph has, by kind and state.

stale.description: Nodes that are `stale`: working, but silent too long.

blocked.description: Unfinished nodes waiting on another node.

Node.title: Node
Node.description:
A session or an agent, as it stood at `as_of_event_id`.

Fields ending `_id` or `_ids` are always present, as ids. The fields beside them without that ending (`parent`, `root`, …), and `children`, `descendants`, `tasks`, `spawns`, `waits` and `messages`, appear only when expanded.

id.description: Unique identifier for the node within its graph: `node_` and the base64url of `provider_ref`.

object.description: String representing the object's type: always `node`.

as_of_event_id.description: The event this node is shown as of.

provider_ref.description: The id the agent tool gave it: `<provider>:<session>` for a session, `<provider>:<session>/<agent>` for an agent. Not an id in this API: use it to match the node to the tool's own records.

provider.description: The agent tool: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, or another that reports to Agent Graph.

parent_id.description: The node it sits under: the agent or session that started it. `null` for a root.

parent.description: The parent node. Present only when expanded.

root_id.description: The top of its tree: follow `parent_id` until it's `null`. A session started by another session is in that session's tree. A root's `root_id` is its own `id`.

root.description: The root node. Present only when expanded.

session_id.description: The session it runs in: itself, for a session; for an agent, the nearest session above it.

session.description: The session node. Present only when expanded.

requested_by_id.description: The node whose spawn request started it, when known. Usually the parent; `null` for a session nothing started, or an agent no request was matched to.

requested_by.description: The node that requested it. Present only when expanded.

depth.description: How far below its root it is: 0 for a root.

stale.description: `working`, waiting on nothing, and silent for 30 minutes: it may have hung or crashed. Measured against `as_of`, not now.

attention.description: While `input_required`: what the person is being asked. Untrusted text.

title.description: The session's name, as its tool shows it. It can change. Untrusted text.

summary.description: Its own latest status line, if it reports one. Untrusted text.

headline.description: One line on what it's doing now: `summary`, else the task in progress. Untrusted text.

purpose.description: Why it was started, from the request that started it. Untrusted text.

agent_type.description: For an agent, its type, as the tool names it (`Explore`, `general-purpose`, …).

background.description: Whether it was started in the background, so its requester carries on without waiting. `null` when unknown.

link_method.description: For a session started by another, how that was worked out: `env` (it inherited its parent's identity), `run` (`agent-graph run` started it), `process` (its parent's agent is among its processes) or `suggested` (it took a name its parent suggested).

spawn_call_id.description: The tool call, in its requester's session, that started it: matches a `spawns[].call_id` on `requested_by`.

cwd.description: The directory it runs in, when reported.

created.description: When it started (or was first seen), in Unix milliseconds.

ended.description: When it finished, in Unix milliseconds. `null` while it hasn't.

last_event.description: When it last had an event, in Unix milliseconds.

child_count.description: How many nodes sit directly under it.

descendant_count.description: How many nodes sit under it, at any depth: the size of `descendants`.

background_agent_count.description: Helpers its tool ran on its own between turns (memory extraction, summaries, prompt suggestions). They report nothing about what they're for, so they're counted, not made nodes.

blocked.description: What it's waiting on, if anything. `null` when it's waiting on nothing, or has finished.

children.description: The nodes directly under it, oldest first: the first 100, and a `url` for the rest. Present only when expanded.

descendants.description: Every node under it, at any depth, as one flat list in tree order: each parent before its children, siblings oldest first. The first 1,000, and a `url` for the rest. Present only when expanded.

tasks.description: Its task list, in the tool's order. Present only when expanded.

spawns.description: The children it has asked for, oldest first. Present only when expanded.

waits.description: What it has waited on and is waiting on, oldest first. Present only when expanded.

messages.description: Messages it has sent and received, oldest first. Present only when expanded.

Blocked.title: Blocked
Blocked.description: What stands between a node and carrying on.

on_ids.description: The nodes it's waiting on directly.

on.description: Those nodes. Present only when `blocked.on` is expanded.

starting.description: Children it has asked for that haven't started yet.

node_count.description: Every unfinished node it's waiting on, directly or through others, with their children.

open_tasks.description: Open tasks across those nodes: the work left before it can carry on.

cycle.description: Its waits lead back to itself: nothing in the loop can ever finish.

Task.title: Task
Task.description: One item on a node's task list.

id.description: The tool's id for the task, unique within the node.

text.description: What the task is. Untrusted text.

active_text.description: How the tool words it while it's in progress (`Running the tests`). Untrusted text.

Spawn.title: Spawn
Spawn.description: A child a node asked for.

call_id.description: The tool call that asked for it.

kind.description: `agent`: an agent in the same session. `session`: a separate session, e.g. `codex exec` run from a shell.

background.description: If false, the requester is blocked until the call returns.

run.description: Whether it's through `agent-graph run`, when known.

title.description: For a session, the name it was to be given.

child_id.description: The node it started, once matched. Before the call returns this can be a best guess, corrected when it does.

requested.description: When it was asked for, in Unix milliseconds.

Wait.title: Wait
Wait.description: A time a node waited on another.

id.description: The wait's id, unique within the node.

kind.description: `spawn`: waiting for a child it asked for, until the call returns. `explicit`: any other wait the tool reported.

on_id.description: The node waited on. `null` while a requested child hasn't started.

started.description: When it started waiting, in Unix milliseconds.

ended.description: When it stopped, in Unix milliseconds.

id.description: The tool's id for the message.

peer_id.description: The node on the other side, when it's one in this graph.

peer_name.description: The tool's name for the other side, when it isn't a node in this graph.

body.description: The whole message, only if the share was made with body capture on. Untrusted text.

created.description: When it was sent, in Unix milliseconds.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: One thing that happened in a graph, and every change it made to its nodes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the event, `evt_…`. Sorts by time.

object.description: String representing the object's type: always `event`.

type.description: What happened. See [event types](#tag/Events). More may be added: ignore those you don't recognise.

created.description: When it happened, in Unix milliseconds.

node.description: That node, as it stood just after this event. Present only when expanded.

payload.description: What the agent tool reported, by `type`: see [event types](#tag/Events). Ids in it are the provider's own. Text in it is untrusted.

changes.description: Every node this event changed, starting with `node_id`. Empty when it changed nothing (a repeated status, say).

payload.purpose: Find every caller of the old session store

provider_version.description: The agent tool's version, when it says.

adapter.description: The Agent Graph adapter that recorded it, and its version, when it says.

NodeChange.title: Node change
NodeChange.description: How one event changed one node.

created.description: Whether the event created it. Its `fields` then go from `null`.

fields.description: Each [node](#tag/Nodes) field that changed, by name, from what to what. Derived fields count (`child_count`, `descendant_count`, `blocked`, `headline`, `task_counts`). `stale` doesn't, as it changes with time rather than events, and nor do expandable fields.

url.description: The URL for this list, with every parameter that defined it (including `as_of`). Add `starting_after` to get the next page.

as_of_event_id.description: Always `null`: each graph has its own history, so each graph carries its own `as_of_event_id`.

has_more.description: Whether there are more after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list, with every parameter that defined it (including `as_of`). Add `starting_after` to get the next page.

as_of_event_id.description: The event the list is as of. Keep it as `as_of` for every page.

has_more.description: Whether there are more after this page.

url.description: The URL for this list, with every parameter that defined it (including `as_of`). Add `starting_after` to get the next page.

as_of_event_id.description: The event the list is as of. Keep it as `as_of` for every page.

has_more.description: Whether there are more after this page.

NodeSearchResult.title: Node search result
NodeSearchResult.description: One page of search results, most recently active first. Pass `next_page` as `page` for the next.

url.description: The URL this result came from.

as_of_event_id.description: The event the search ran as of. Every page of one search runs as of the same event.

next_page.description: The cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page.

total_count.description: How many nodes match in all.

code.description: A short string saying exactly what went wrong: see [errors](#section/Errors). More may be added.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person to read. It may change: branch on `code`, not on this.

param.description: The parameter the error is about, if any.

doc_url.description: Where this error code is explained.

first_event_id.description: With `outside_retention_window`: the oldest event the graph holds. With `node_not_yet_created`: the event that creates the node.

last_event_id.description: With `outside_retention_window`: the newest event the graph holds.
